2866.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂yu-gʷih₃- (“long life”) or Proto-Indo-European *h₁su-gʷih₃- (“good life”) with -ής (-ḗs, “adjective suffix”); the former derivation is favored by Beekes and Weiss.

2800.t: From τιμωρός (tīmōrós, “avenging, avenger”) + -έω (-éō, denominative verbal suffix), a contraction of τιμάορος (tīmáoros), from τιμή (tīmḗ, “honour”) + ὁράω (horáō, “to see”).

2872.t: Of uncertain origin. Could be related to ῥώομαι (rhṓomai, “I dart”), as well as Sanskrit सार (sā́ra, “strength, power, energy”), which would hypothetically trace back to a Proto-Indo-European *serh₃- (“power; to move violently”).

2826.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hagnós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁yáǵ-nós, from *h₁yaǵ- (“to sacrifice; to worship”). Cognate with Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hyaȷ́nás.

2855.t: From Old Median; see Old Persian 𐏃𐎥𐎶𐎫𐎠𐎴 (Hangmatāna) for more.

2831.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *árguros. Further from a u-stem of Proto-Indo-European *h₂erǵ- (“white; argent”).

2824.t: From Proto-Hellenic *warḗn, from Proto-Indo-European *wr̥h₁ḗn (“lamb”). Cognates include Latin vervēx (“wether”), Sanskrit उर॑ण (úraṇa) and Old Armenian գառն (gaṙn).

2861.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hοrmā́, with two plausible derivations: * From Proto-Indo-European *sor-meh₂- (“flow, stream”), from *ser- (“to flow, stream”), and thus cognate with Sanskrit सर्म (sárma, “going, running, flowing”), from the verb सरति (sarati, “to…

2810.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéweti, from *ǵʰew- (“to pour”). Cognates include Sanskrit जुहोति (juhóti), Old Armenian ձեւ (jew), Latin fundō, fūtis, Old English ġēotan, guttas (English gut), and Albanian dyllë.

2862.t: Traditionally held to be related to ὀστέον (ostéon, “bone”) and ὄστρεον (óstreon, “oyster”). Beekes considers it more likely to be Pre-Greek, which does not exclude a relation to ὄστρεον (óstreon).

2802.t: τόξον (tóxon, “bow”) + -της (-tēs, masculine suffix for person concerned with something)

2804.t: Disputed. From a root *bʰaḱ- shared with Albanian bathë (“broad bean”).

2887.t: Said by Beekes to be a Mediterranean wanderwort; substrate common to μαντία (mantía, “blackberry”) (Dacian loan), and Albanian man (“mulberry”), Gheg mand.

2860.t: From Proto-Hellenic *omíkʰlā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃migʰleh₂. Cognate with Lithuanian miglà (“mist, haze”), Sanskrit मेघ (meghá, “cloud, gloomy weather”), Old Armenian մէգ (mēg, “mist”) and Albanian mjegull (“fog; haze”).

2827.t: Stem ἁδ- as in the root of adverb ἅδην (hádēn), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂- (“to fill up, satiate, satisfy”) + -ρός (-rós).

2813.t: From ἄγρυπνος (ágrupnos, “sleepless, wakeful”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun suffix).

2840.t: From ἐλέφας (eléphas, “elephant”) + -ινος (-inos, “-ine”). Compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀩𐀞𐀳𐀃 (e-re-pa-te-o), 𐀁𐀩𐀞𐀳𐀍 (e-re-pa-te-jo, “made of ivory”) formed with -εῖος (-eîos).

2808.t: According to Beekes, of unknown or Pre-Greek origin, and unrelated to Armenian խաղ (xaġ, “game, pastime”) (a connection would require a Proto-Indo-European *kʰ, which is unheard of for inherited words).

2809.t: Suppletive comparative of κακός (kakós, “bad”), from an element χερ- (kher-) of disputed origin + comparative suffix *-ϳων (*-jōn).

2870.t: From some Semitic source. Compare Akkadian 𒍪𒌑𒁍 (/⁠zūpu⁠/), Jewish Palestinian Aramaic אֵיזוֹבָא (ʾēzôḇa), Hebrew אֵזוֹב (ʾēzṓḇ), Classical Syriac ܙܘܦܐ (zōṗā).

2882.t: According to Beekes, probably of Pre-Greek origin and cognate with βλέπω (blépō, “to see, to perceive”). Hamp had suggested Proto-Indo-European *gʷlep- (“to look”), though he offers no extra-Hellenic comparanda for such a root.

2856.t: From ἡδύνω (hēdúnō, “to season”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

2835.t: From Proto-Hellenic *həl͏̌l͏̌omai, from Proto-Indo-European *sl̥yétor, from the root *sel-. Cognate with Latin saliō (“to jump”) and Sanskrit सरति (sárati, “to run”).

2852.t: Of uncertain relation outside of Greek. Sometimes compared to Latin ridica (“vine-prop, stake”), but De Vaan finds this connection shaky at best.

2807.t: A technical word without etymology, so possibly Pre-Greek.

2806.t: It has been assumed a derivation with a reduced grade from φέρω (phérō, “to carry”), beside a full grade in φέρετρον (phéretron, “bier, litter”).

2833.t: Related to ἐξαίφνης (exaíphnēs), αἴφνης (aíphnēs, “suddenly”), ἐξαπίνης (exăpínēs, “id”), of uncertain origin.

2821.t: From ἀ- (a-, “without”) + νοέω (noéō, “to perceive”) + -τός (-tós, adjectival suffix).
